title: Investigation 01: Microsoft Security Alert
subject: Unusual sign-in activity detected
scenario: You receive two Microsoft security notifications. Email A arrives from account-security@microsoft.com and advises you to review recent sign-in activity through your usual Microsoft account portal. Email B arrives from security@micros0ft-account.example and asks you to verify your password immediately using an unfamiliar link. Compare both messages and identify the genuine security notification.
email_note: Microsoft security notifications should be verified through the official Microsoft account portal.
options: Email A is legitimate and Email B is phishing.
Email B is legitimate and Email A is phishing.
Both emails are legitimate.
Both emails are phishing.
explanation: Email A uses the legitimate microsoft.com domain and directs the employee to the official security portal. Email B uses a lookalike domain containing a zero instead of the letter 'o'. Never trust a sender name alone.

title: Investigation 02: Fake Fuji Silvertech Password Reset
subject: URGENT: Your Fuji Account Will Be Deactived
scenario:
Dear Employee,

Your Fuji Silvertech account will be deactived today due to a security issue. Please complet the password verfication process within 30 minutes to avoid account suspension.

Click the link below to confirm your account details:

https://fuji-silvertec-secure.example/login

You must enter your current password and MFA code to restore access.

Thank you,
Fuji Silvertech IT Support
email_note: Examine the sender address, spelling, link and requests for confidential information. Select the suspicious items.

mistakes.text: The sender address uses fuji-silvertec-secure.example instead of the official fujisilvertech.com domain.
The words 'deactived', 'complet' and 'verfication' contain spelling errors.
The email creates a 30-minute deadline and asks for the employee's password and MFA code.

explanation: The sender uses an unofficial domain, the message contains spelling mistakes, and it creates urgency while requesting credentials and an MFA code. Genuine IT support should never ask employees to disclose passwords or MFA codes.

title: Investigation 03: Suspicious Shared Document
subject: A confidential document has been shared with you
scenario:
Hello,

A confidential company document has been shared with you. You must open and verify this document within 30 minutes or your access will be permanently removed.

Open the document here:

https://sharepoint-access.example/verify-document

To continue, enter your company password and MFA verification code. Do not contact IT because this is an automated security verification.

Regards,
Document Sharing Service
email_note: Find the three suspicious indicators in this email.

mistakes.text: The sender and document link use an unverified sharepoint-access.example domain.
The message threatens permanent access removal within 30 minutes.
The email requests the company password and MFA code and discourages contacting IT.

explanation: The three indicators are the unverified sender and link domain, artificial urgency, and the request for credentials combined with discouraging independent verification. Always verify unexpected document-sharing invitations through an official company channel.

title: Investigation 04: Suspicious HR Salary Revision
subject: URGENT: Salery Revision Confirmation Required
scenario:
Dear Team Member,

Your annual salery revision has been approved. Please compleate the employee confirmation form immediately to ensure that your revised compensation is included in the next payroll cycle.

Click here to confirm your details:

https://fujisilvertech-careers.example/payroll-confirm

You are required to enter your employee ID, bank account details and payroll password.

Regards,
Human Resourses Department
email_note: Check the sender domain, spelling and information requested. Select the suspicious items.

mistakes.text: The sender uses fujisilvertech-careers.example instead of the official fujisilvertech.com domain.
The email contains spelling errors such as 'salery', 'compleate' and 'Resourses'.
The email requests bank account details and a payroll password through an unfamiliar link.

explanation: The sender domain is not the official company domain, the message contains spelling errors, and it requests sensitive banking and password information. Verify salary and payroll changes directly with HR using known contact details.

title: Investigation 05: Official Client Report
subject: Updated Client Report - Review Required
scenario:
Dear Team,

The updated client report for this week's review is ready. Please review the attached document and share any corrections by Thursday at 3:00 PM.

The document is available through the company's approved document-sharing platform. If you have any trouble accessing it, please contact the project coordination team.

Regards,
Project Coordination Team
email_note: This is an example of a routine internal business communication.
options: Report the email immediately because all document links are phishing attempts.
Treat it as a legitimate business email, while checking the attachment and link before opening.
Forward the email to an external personal account for review.
Reply with your company password to confirm access.
explanation: The message uses the official company domain, provides a normal business deadline and directs employees to a company platform. However, employees should still verify unexpected attachments and links before opening them.

title: Investigation 06: The Difficult Policy Update
subject: Mandatory Security Policy Review
scenario: You receive an email from an address that appears to belong to the official company domain. It contains your correct department name, employee designation and a reference to a recent security policy update. The email asks you to review a policy document hosted on a third-party website. The sender says the document is approved by the Information Security Office. The link opens a page that requests your company login credentials. What should you do?
email_note: This scenario tests whether you can identify a suspicious request even when the sender and message appear convincing.
options: Trust the email because the sender address and employee details look correct.
Enter your credentials because the email references a genuine company policy update.
Do not enter credentials. Independently verify the request with the Information Security Office using an approved company channel.
Forward the link to colleagues so they can confirm whether it works.
explanation: A convincing sender address and accurate employee information do not prove that a message is safe. The unexpected third-party login page is a major warning sign. Verify the request independently through an approved channel before interacting with the link.

title: Investigation 07: The HR Benefits Announcement
subject: New Employee Benefits - Registration Open
scenario: A message is shared in a company group chat announcing new employee benefits. It asks employees to complete a registration form through an unfamiliar external website. The message claims that registration will close today and that employees who do not complete the form will lose their benefits. The sender is not a verified HR representative.
email_note: Think about how employees should verify benefits-related announcements.
options: Complete the form immediately because the benefits deadline is today.
Share the form with the entire team so everyone can register.
Verify the announcement with HR through an official company channel before submitting personal information.
Enter your employee credentials to check whether the form is genuine.
explanation: Benefits announcements should be verified with HR through official communication channels. Unverified forms, external websites and pressure-based deadlines can be used to collect personal information.

title: Investigation 08: Fake Google Storage Warning
subject: Your Google Storage Is Almost Full - Action Requird
scenario:
Dear User,

Your company Google storage is almost full. Your account may stop recieving emails and sharing documents unless you upgrade your storage immediatly.

Click below to increase your storage:

https://google-workspace-quota.example/upgrade

To continue, please enter your company email password and payment details.

Failure to complete this process today may result in permanent data loss.

Regards,
Google Workspace Storage Team
email_note: Inspect the sender, spelling, link and request for sensitive information. Select the suspicious items.

mistakes.text: The sender and link use google-workspace-quota.example instead of a verified Google domain.
The message contains spelling errors such as 'requird', 'recieving' and 'immediatly'.
The email requests an account password and payment details while threatening permanent data loss.

explanation: The sender and link use an unverified domain, the message contains spelling mistakes, and it requests passwords and payment details while creating fear of data loss. Check storage status directly through your organization's approved Google Workspace portal.

title: Investigation 09: Official Vendor Payment Confirmation
subject: Vendor Payment Processing Confirmation
scenario:
Dear Team,

This is to confirm that the approved vendor payment request has been received by the Accounts Payable Department. The payment will be processed according to the existing payment schedule.

For any questions regarding the status of the transaction, please contact the Accounts Payable team through the company's official contact directory.

Regards,
Accounts Payable Department
email_note: Review the sender and the payment-related instructions before deciding.
options: Treat it as a legitimate internal confirmation, while verifying any payment changes through the approved finance process.
Immediately transfer another payment to confirm the transaction.
Reply with banking credentials to help Accounts Payable process the payment.
Report it as phishing because all payment-related emails are fraudulent.
explanation: The message comes from the official company domain and does not request credentials, new bank details or an urgent transfer. It directs employees to the official contact directory. Any change to vendor payment details must still be independently verified.

title: Investigation 10: Executive Impersonation
subject: Confidential - Immediate Action Required
scenario: You receive an email claiming to be from the CEO. The sender says they are in an important meeting and cannot take calls. They ask you to purchase gift cards for a client and send the redemption codes immediately. The email says the request is confidential and must not be discussed with anyone else.
email_note: Executive impersonation attacks often use authority, secrecy and urgency to pressure employees.
options: Purchase the gift cards immediately because the request comes from the CEO.
Reply asking the sender to confirm the gift card amounts.
Independently verify the request with the executive through a known company communication channel and report the suspicious email.
Send the gift card codes first and verify the request afterward.
explanation: This is a common business email compromise technique. Attackers impersonate senior executives and use authority, urgency and secrecy to pressure employees into transferring money or gift card codes. Always verify unusual financial requests through a separate trusted channel.
